name: Sar'theris Strand
summary: Along western Desolace, Sar'theris Strand's green shores meet the Veiled Sea. Its sunny grass stands apart from the grey wastes, though naga, sea giants, and makrura make the coast perilous.

sections.title: A Green Edge on a Grey Waste
sections.body: Green clifftops and beaches mark Sar'theris Strand along western Desolace. They offer a bright respite from the ash and dust of the inland plains. Serpentine naga patrol the surf beside towering sea giants and territorial makrura. Wrecks mark the shoals: the ruined Karnitol vessel lies to the north, and small shattered skiffs rest beneath the towers of Ethel Rethor. The sea is as treacherous as the shore.

sections.title: Wreckage and Rare Waters
sections.body: Naga and sea giants are not the strand's only dangers. Jagged shallows hide salvage from lost expeditions and merchant ventures, while rare marine life dwells in the deep surf. Among it is the Sar'theris Striker, a fish sought by master fishermen across Kalimdor.

faq.q: Why is Sar'theris Strand green when the rest of Desolace is dead?
faq.answer: Sar'theris Strand is sunny and grassy, unlike Desolace's barren grey interior. No reason for the contrast is given.

aliases: what monsters are on the strand
faq.answer: Amphibious Slitherblade naga, wandering sea giants, and scuttling makrura inhabit the strand. Their patrols roam near the water's edge, so watch the surf.

faq.q: What shipwrecks lie along the shore?
faq.answer: The Karnitol Shipwreck lies in the strand's northern waters. Smaller vessels are smashed on the beach bluffs beneath the ruined elven towers of Ethel Rethor.

faq.q: Why do fishermen seek out Sar'theris Strand?
faq.answer: Fishermen seek Sar'theris Strand for the Sar'theris Striker, an elusive fish found only in these coastal waters. Renowned angler Nat Pagle recognizes it as one of fishing mastery’s ultimate tests.

angles.text: Sar'theris Strand's shores and waters offer marine game, including makrura and rare ocean fish. Watch for prowling naga when you light a cooking fire.
